engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC 15537895); full text PMC6730192 not read.
engagement.note: Single intraputaminal AAV5-NaGlu in 6-week Naglu-/- mice gave brain-wide NaGlu activity above physiological levels; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: Mouse brain NaGlu after AAV, pre-clinic
engagement.quote: High NaGlu activity, far above physiological levels, was measured in the brain and persisted at 38 weeks of age.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the Paris group's mouse study chose AAV5 over AAV2 for the intracerebral route later used with rAAV2/5-hNAGLU; a separate system from the draft's dog track and from the mouse IV/ICV enzyme tracks.

engagement.magnitude_basis: brain (mouse) vs lumbar CSF (patient) NAGLU activity after intracerebral AAV
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; n=4; ISRCTN19853672/NCT03300453 have no posted results. Patient quote taken from the draft's verified Tardieu 2017 entry.
engagement.note: Children given intracerebral rAAV2/5-hNAGLU had CSF NAGLU at 15-20% of unaffected children, as the mouse brain expression predicted.
engagement.short: CSF NAGLU detected in all 4 children
engagement.quote: NAGLU activity was detected in lumbar CSF and was 15-20% of that in unaffected children.
engagement.reason: Transgene NAGLU expressed in patients' CNS
engagement.judgement: Paired: mouse brain enzyme vs patient CSF enzyme; direction matches, levels not comparable (mouse supraphysiological, patients below normal).

efficacy.note: Treated Naglu-/- mice behaved normally and lost most storage vacuolation, though improvement was partial in some animals.
efficacy.quote: These results indicate that NaGlu delivery from intracerebral sources has the capacity to alleviate most disease manifestations in the MPSIIIB mouse model.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry: the mouse predicts that intracerebral NAGLU expression prevents neurological disease.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: developmental quotient decline vs natural history
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; uncontrolled n=4 against natural history; registered primary was safety. Quote from the draft's verified Tardieu 2017 entry.
efficacy.note: All four children still declined but less than natural history at 30 months; youngest near normal.
efficacy.quote: Compared with the natural history of mucopolysaccharidosis type III syndromes, neurocognitive progression was improved in all patients, with the youngest patient having function close to that in healthy children.
efficacy.judgement: Scored on the neurocognitive secondary as the draft does for the dog track (only efficacy readout); partial because decline slowed rather than stopped.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: brain atrophy and neurocognition vs untreated Sanfilippo A/B children at 5.5 years
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC 34405688); n=4, uncontrolled; efficacy was the secondary endpoint; the youngest patient did better than untreated children.
efficacy.note: At 5.5 years, 3 of 4 children had brain atrophy and neurocognition no different from untreated Sanfilippo children despite persistent CSF NAGLU.
efficacy.short: No benefit in 3 of 4 at 5.5 y
efficacy.quote: Patients 2, 3, and 4 showed progressive brain atrophy and neurocognitive evolution that did not differ from untreated Sanfilippo A/B children.
efficacy.reason: Benefit not sustained in older children
efficacy.judgement: Long-term follow-up of the same trial overturns the 30-month signal in 3 of 4 patients, so the mouse prediction of alleviating most disease manifestations is contradicted; the youngest patient's milder course keeps confidence low. The checker flagged the same datum for the dog track.

added_models.model: MPS IIIB dog, ICV tralesinidase alfa (20 months)

dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9426762, BioC) read. Opening year 2016 is a proxy (trial start April 2016), as on this track's engagement entry.
dose.note: 20-month ICV study in MPS IIIB dogs at 12 and 48 mg every other week; dose scaled to humans by brain mass.
dose.short: Dog dose scaled by brain mass
dose.quote: Therefore, one appropriate method to scale doses across species to estimate an efficacious dose for human patients is to correct for brain mass.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the dog track's dose cell; the dog study stated both an effective-dose estimate and a tolerability margin, published 2022.

dose.magnitude_basis: dog-predicted effective clinical dose (300 mg weekly, CSF HS normalization) vs dose that normalized patient CSF HS (300 mg)
dose.confidence_note: Dog full text read; Muschol 2023 full text quote from the draft's verified engagement entry. NCT02754076 has no posted results (checked). Subject to rule question 3 on margins published after trial start.
dose.note: Dogs tolerated 48 mg (about 960 mg every other week human-equivalent), a stated margin over 300 mg weekly; patients reached CSF HS normalization at 300 mg.
dose.short: 300 mg normalized CSF HS, margin held
dose.quote: In the Part 1 dose escalation (30, 100, and 300 mg) phase, a 300 mg dose of tralesinidase alfa was necessary to achieve normalization of HS and HS-NRE levels in the CSF and plasma.
dose.reason: 300 mg reached HS target; margin held
dose.judgement: Dog paper states 48 mg 'provides a sufficient safety margin over the clinical dose (300 mg weekly)' and 300 mg 'should normalize HS'; patients reached that at 300 mg and were kept on it. Partial: drug-related CSF pleocytosis SAEs (counted in safety). Same rule question as dose 4 (cyno-icv-ta-tox): margin published 2022, after the 2016 trial start but before patient data (2023); if the adjudicator rules such margins inadmissible, this becomes untested.

considered_not_added: MPS I (Hurler) dog, intracerebral rAAV2/5 (source of the vector dose): reported in Ellinwood 2011, the draft's dog paper; no human dose target stated and no separate patient comparison
Naglu-/- mouse, AAV8/AAV9 vectors (Heldermon 2013, Gilkes 2016/2021, Rouse 2023) and ABO-101 (AAV9-NAGLU): products outside the member list; no member-drug patient comparison
SBC-103 nonclinical toxicology (rat/NHP): not published; no patient comparison found
Patient fibroblasts / iPSC-derived neural cells (Yogalingam 2019 BMN 250 uptake; Huang 2021 patient iPSC model): no comparison with patient results
Human genetic model (attenuated NAGLU variants with residual activity as an enzyme-threshold predictor): no source compares it with treated patients
In-silico / PK / allometric model for tralesinidase alfa or SBC-103 dose: none found

Dog ICV tralesinidase dose margin (Ellinwood 2022) and Deiva 2021 data for the dog AAV track: belong to tracks the draft already has (checker 'missing'), not new systems; this file does not edit the draft
